🤖 Anthropic launches Claude Science for research

Anthropic introduced Claude Science, an AI agent designed as an end-to-end research infrastructure. It handles literature search, data analysis, computation, visualization, and article preparation in one interface.

Claude Science comes with a built-in skill base and offers various visualizations and artifact displays. It is currently in beta and available as an app for MacOS and Linux.

🤖 OpenAI launches Codex Micro keyboard

OpenAI released the Codex Micro, a $230 keyboard made with Work Louder for users of its AI agent Codex. It has six large keys, each linked to a separate agent and showing status by color: blue means working, green means task done, orange means waiting for human input.

The keyboard lets users switch agents with one press or open the Codex window with two. Codex has over 8 million weekly users, many running multiple agents at once.

Managing several agents on screen is tricky, so OpenAI built this device to track their states physically. It doesn’t write code but helps users handle multiple AI agents simultaneously.

🔥Real Steel has officially become reality

China has launched Ultimate Robot Knockout Legend (URKL), a full-fledged fighting league where humanoid robots step into the ring and battle for glory.

The tournament features 16 teams, but everyone uses the exact same robot. There are no hardware advantages.

The winner is decided by software.

Each team develops its own AI, control algorithms, movement, balance, reflexes, and fighting strategy, turning every match into a battle of engineering rather than expensive hardware.

💰 There’s also serious money on the line: a 10 million yuan (around $1.4 million) prize pool.

And the fights are already delivering unforgettable moments.

In one of the first matches, a robot gets completely decapitated after taking a huge hit… then simply gets back up and keeps fighting like nothing happened. 🤯

The commentators couldn’t help but laugh: “Well… now the opponent can’t score any more headshots.”

Even better, watch until the end, the winning robot actually celebrates its victory, making it look like a scene straight out of Real Steel.

This isn’t just entertainment. It’s also a showcase of how far robotics and AI have come.

Would you pay to watch robot fights instead of human MMA? 🤔

🗣"AI is like oil." Chamath's latest take on All-In is the simplest explanation of why AI pricing is about to collapse.

He said think of one million AI tokens as one barrel of intelligence.

Anthropic sells that barrel for $56. OpenAI sells it for $26. Elon sells it for $1. Zuck sells it for $1.50. Google sells it for $1. The Chinese sell it for 50 cents.

Same barrel. Wildly different prices.

His point: "If you've made a bet around one of these folks selling extremely expensive barrels of intelligence, you may run into some downstream
difficulty."

The capability gap between the expensive models and the cheap ones is shrinking every month. The pricing gap hasn't caught up yet. When it does, someone's margins collapse.

🇯🇵 Japanese Robot Floats Like a Living Whale

Engineers at Keio University created a small white robot that silently floats in the air using a helium-filled shell. This design supports most of its weight, letting motors only steer it, which cuts energy use and noise.

The robot moves with soft flapping fins instead of propellers, making it safer and more lifelike. It can gently push, touch, or even hug, and it navigates spaces under ceilings, over furniture, and up stairs.

🤖 OpenAI chairman Bret Taylor talks to about 100 CEOs every month. 

His answer to the cheap open-weight model panic: cheaper to train does not mean cheaper to use, and the number that decides it is token efficiency.

"One thing that I think is a little bit overblown about these open weight models is they're not necessarily cheaper to run. Whether or not they're cheaper to train, you don't care. Because you're using just as many tokens. In fact, they may be less efficient."

"There's this thing called token efficiency. And it turns out the frontier models are much, much more token efficient."

"A token is to intelligence like a watt is to electricity... how many tokens does it take to complete a task? Not every token is actually equal."

"For a lot of tasks, it turns out these frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic are actually just better than these open weight models... just having open weights isn't actually the main thing driving any of those costs."

Later in the same interview he goes after the billing unit itself: "It would be like if you signed up for Gmail and you paid for CPU cycle or something... where the world is going is paying for outcomes."

The unresolved column: the chart CNBC airs mid-answer, from Artificial Analysis, prices a completed task at $0.94 on Kimi K3 against $2.75 on Claude Fable 5, efficiency folded in. If that gap holds, the premium he is defending gets earned on quality, not price.

Sam Altman has reportedly stated that "we are now in the singularity." This term refers to a hypothetical point when artificial intelligence surpasses human intelligence, fundamentally changing technology and society.

Despite this claim, the majority of people outside specialized technology circles remain unaware of these developments. Most do not yet understand the significance or potential impact of such advancements.

🗣Kimi CEO: "AI is Accelerating Faster Than Ever. A new Scaling Era has Begun."

- AI is improving in two dimensions, vertical scaling and horizontal scaling.

- Reasoning has advanced dramatically. AI now solves complex math and coding tasks that were nearly impossible just a year ago.

- Context windows have exploded from roughly 4K to 8K tokens to 128K+ tokens, allowing models to understand far longer documents and conversations.

- Progress is no longer driven only by larger models. Better post-training, reinforcement learning, higher-quality data and inference-time reasoning are now accelerating capabilities.

- Multimodal AI is advancing rapidly. Systems can now generate videos, transform research papers into realistic podcasts and seamlessly work across text, images, audio and video.

- OpenAI's o1 introduced a new paradigm. Experts described it as AI demonstrating System 2 reasoning, enabling deliberate thinking, self-correction, exploration of multiple solution paths, and reflection.

- A new scaling law has emerged. Beyond pre-training, reinforcement learning and inference-time search now provide another predictable path for improving intelligence.

- AGI has entered a new stage. According to Professor Ju Jun's framework, AI has moved from L1 Chatbots toward L2 Reasoners, representing a major qualitative leap.

- Zhilin Yang (CEO of Kimi): "The most important significance is that it raises the upper limit of what AI can achieve."

- Professor Ju Jun: "The progress curve is getting steeper and steeper."

- Industry experts: "We're in the middle of an acceleration process, and the pace of AI development is still increasing."

🎤 ChatGPT voice is becoming your computer’s AI command center

OpenAI has upgraded ChatGPT Voice from a voice assistant into a hands-free control system for your computer.

Powered by GPT-Live, the feature lets you talk naturally while ChatGPT launches tasks, monitors progress, and coordinates multiple AI agents running across ChatGPT Work and Codex. Your conversation continues while those agents work in the background, and ChatGPT can explain what’s happening, report results, and take new instructions, all without sending you back to the keyboard.

On macOS, it goes even further. ChatGPT can understand the app currently on your screen using screen context, and after pairing your iPhone with your Mac, you can leave your desk and continue managing tasks remotely with your voice.

The update is rolling out globally for Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise users on both macOS and Windows.

🧠 Demis Hassabis says DeepMind had no choice but to sell.

Before AI became a trillion-dollar race, DeepMind was struggling to survive. Demis Hassabis says he realized staying independent would require $7 billion in funding.

The problem? They could barely raise $10 million at a time. After DeepMind’s breakthrough Atari demos, Big Tech started aggressively recruiting its researchers.

They had no product, no revenue, and were focused entirely on building AGI. Hassabis says he paid himself nothing, while engineers earning around $100,000 a year were suddenly receiving offers of $10 million… or even $50 million annually.

At that point, competing as an independent company became almost impossible. That’s why DeepMind joined Google in 2014. Looking back, it wasn’t just a business decision.

It was a reminder that building frontier AI has always been as much about capital and talent as it is about breakthrough research.

🤖 OpenAI is giving away GPT-5.6 to 100,000 researchers for free.

OpenAI has launched ChatGPT for Academic Researchers, a new program that gives scientists, mathematicians, and engineers free access to its frontier AI models.

The rollout starts with 10,000 researchers and will expand to 100,000 by 2027.

Participants get access to the GPT-5.6 family, business-grade privacy (their data isn’t used to train models by default), support for up to 4 collaborators, plus training and hands-on guidance.

The goal? Help researchers spend less time on paperwork and more time making discoveries, from writing grant proposals to testing new ideas.

❗️Peter Thiel thinks we got AI completely backwards

For years, everyone assumed AI would replace writers, marketers, and people in the humanities first. Peter Thiel wasn’t convinced. His argument is that people most at risk were mathematicians.

At first, that sounded crazy. Today, it doesn’t. Math is almost the perfect playground for AI:

• Every problem has a way to verify the answer. The model instantly knows if it’s right or wrong.

• It can explore millions of possible solution paths in seconds, something no human can match.

• The feedback loop is immediate. Find a proof, verify it, learn from it, repeat. That’s exactly the kind of cycle AI improves at incredibly fast.

Writing is different. Good writing isn’t just about being correct. It’s about taste, context, emotion, timing, culture, and knowing what not to say. There isn’t always a single right answer, which makes improvement much messier.

And now we’re seeing the evidence.

AI is helping generate original mathematical proofs at a pace that would have seemed impossible just a few years ago. Problems that once defined PhD-level research are increasingly being tackled by frontier models.

😐 Jensen Huang wants to outlive himself

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says he’s already building an AI version of himself.

His plan? Upload everything he’s ever written, said, and created into an AI, then one day beam that digital “Jensen” to a humanoid robot already waiting in space. 

To Huang, your body is just the hardware. The real “you” is the information.

He also believes we’re much closer to solving biology than most people think, predicting that within about five years we’ll understand the human body well enough to dramatically accelerate cures for diseases like cancer and Alzheimer’s. In his words, the “end of disease” is a reasonable expectation.

And he’s just as optimistic about the future beyond Earth, saying cleaner energy, faster space travel, even eventually traveling at the speed of light, are all within humanity’s reach.

Despite building the chips powering today’s AI revolution, Huang says his biggest bet isn’t on technology, it’s on people. He believes humans are fundamentally kind, creative, and far more likely to build than destroy.

His final thought summed it all up perfectly: “How can you not be romantic about that?”

🗣"Superintelligence won't arrive all at once. It will emerge through automation."

Andrej Karpathy says superintelligence is best understood as the long-term continuation of automation.

First, AI automates digital work. Then physical work. Eventually, even scientific discovery, invention, and decision making become increasingly automated.

The biggest challenge may not be a single AI taking over.

It could be a gradual loss of human understanding and control as billions of autonomous AI systems interact, compete, and make decisions at a scale and speed no human can fully comprehend.

Superintelligence may not look like one all-powerful AI. It may look like an economy of autonomous intelligences.

🙃 Elon Musk: “Consciousness isn’t a switch, it’s a continuum”

Elon Musk just challenged one of the biggest assumptions in the AI debate: there may never be a single moment when AI suddenly becomes “conscious.”

His argument is simple. Humans don’t wake up one day as conscious beings. A zygote isn’t conscious in the same way an adult is, and no one can point to the exact day they crossed that invisible line. Consciousness appears to grow gradually, not arrive all at once.

If that’s true, Musk says we’re asking the wrong question about AI. We’ve been waiting for a dramatic “awakening”, a clear moment when a machine crosses the line. But what if there is no line? What if consciousness is a spectrum, and AI is simply moving along it with every new model, training run, and architectural breakthrough?

He then zooms out even further.

The universe began with quarks, leptons, and hydrogen. Over billions of years, stars forged the heavier elements that eventually became planets, life, and us. The atoms in our bodies were once inside stars. In Musk’s view, humans aren’t separate from that process, we’re simply one stage of it.

Now, those same atoms have built machines capable of learning, reasoning, and creating.

It could solve humanity's biggest problems. Or create existential ones.

The same intelligence that unlocks abundance could determine the future.

🤖 ChatGPT adds Computer History on Mac

The desktop ChatGPT app for Mac now includes Computer History, which tracks your activity in apps and websites to provide context in future chats. It can recall recent tasks, find documents, and continue work without needing repeated explanations.

Computer History logs events like clicks, text input, and app switching without recording screen, mic, or system audio. Data stays on the Mac for up to 48 hours and users can pause or delete history selectively.

Built on an updated version of Chronicle, the feature uses fewer tokens and offers more privacy controls. It is off by default and rolling out to Pro, Business, and Enterprise users.
